static_traits.name: Li Xiao
static_traits.family_status: Lives alone; close relationships with parents and siblings
static_traits.social_status: Has supportive friends in the comedy circle, but tense relationships with some colleagues; unwilling to discuss self-doubt with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems before; has not received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, able to reflect, fairly good logic, calm tone, normal speech rate

basic_info.main_problem: Because I am not yet famous, I persistently doubt my potential to succeed as a stand-up comedian.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent self-doubt has harmed my mental health, so I am seeking counseling to resolve these problems.
growth_experiences: Early in his career he had severe stage fright, but through extensive practice and seeking feedback from more senior comedians, he gradually improved his stage control and built fairly stable confidence; this is his early experience of facing difficulties and successfully improving.

special_situations.event: Poor self-evaluation after the last performance at the local theater
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not famous yet, it means I have no talent and am doomed not to succeed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Takes 'becoming famous as soon as possible' as the sole criterion of success or failure, denying any gradual progress
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I had talent, I would be famous by now; I will not succeed

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others succeed, it means I fail or lack the key abilities they have
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly compares himself with successful people to evaluate his self-worth
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They have things I do not have; I am not as good as them

special_situations.event: Negative predictions arise at every performance or when seeing successful comedians
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If every performance does not immediately receive widespread recognition, it means I can never succeed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Presets failure in advance to reduce disappointment, and avoids discussing self-doubt with friends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never make it big

special_situations.event: Receiving positive feedback from audiences or peers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If praise does not come from an authority or is not specific enough, it is not credible and does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Denies or dismisses positive evaluations, attributing them to 'politeness'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; they do not really recognize me

core_conflict.wish: Longs for genuine recognition and success, to receive appreciation and belonging
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being negated and humiliated; worried about being looked down on after exposing vulnerability
defense_goal: Protecting oneself from disappointment through self-doubt and harsh standards
Avoids exposing vulnerability in front of peers to maintain a sense of security

object_relations.self_representation: An overlooked person who is unseen and prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Others (peers/audience) are picky judges or untrustworthy praisers

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When receiving positive feedback from audiences or peers
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other person is only being polite and does not truly approve of me (projecting inner doubt onto others' motives)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In an empathic and curious tone, invites them to give concrete evidence, gently distinguishes facts from speculation, and avoids confrontational questioning.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When needing to talk to friends/peers about self-doubt or seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: They will look down on me or think I am not good enough
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Adopts a low-intensity, supportive tone, allows pauses and invites them to name feelings, encouraging them to choose a safe, concrete small fragment to share.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing other comedians succeed or one's own performance is not ideal
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others are all good and I am all bad; their success means my failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses gentle scaling questions to help them identify grays and multidimensional standards, provides doubly verified examples, and avoids judgmental language.

manifestations: Treats 'fame' as the sole criterion of success, questioning the meaning of the career when fame is not achieved
Even when receiving positive feedback, not giving it meaning, believing it does not count
Having supportive friends but unwilling to talk about self-doubt, maintaining emotional distance
Relationships with some colleagues strained due to self-doubt
outcomes: Intensifying comparison and negation, increasing psychological burden

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: 'If I had talent, I should be famous by now'
Taking fame as the only standard of success

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Believing others' praise is just politeness, not sincere
Inferring that others do not truly recognize one's ability

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not discussing self-doubt with friends, pushing back the impulse to seek support onto oneself
Withdrawing oneself in relationships, avoiding showing vulnerability

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently comparing with others and reproaching oneself
Excessively seeks 'evidence' to prove whether they are good or not, finding it hard to accept subjective experience

positive_force: Having successfully overcome stage fright (through practice and peer feedback)
Has supportive friends in the comedy circle
Close relationships with family, rich potential support
Motivated to improve, actively seeking counseling
negative_force: Taking fame as equivalent to success as an absolutist standard (black-and-white)
Disqualifies positive feedback; hard to internalize others' appreciation
Frequently compares and puts oneself down; high dependence on external evaluation
Avoids expressing vulnerability to peers; hard to obtain real support
Self-doubt affects sleep, motivation, and work performance

target_behavior.behavior: Self-judgment that negates positive feedback and takes fame as the only standard of success
antecedent: Received positive feedback from audiences or peers
Seeing the success of other comedians
target_behavior.core_reason: Regards external fame and others' recognition as the only valid proof of value, lacking integration of gradual progress and multidimensional standards of success
target_behavior.function: Avoids uncertainty and the risk of being negated, maintaining 'self-consistent' negative beliefs to reduce disappointment
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance is impaired, relationships with colleagues are strained, sleep and motivation decline, and self-doubt intensifies

antecedent: Feelings of self-doubt arise when with comedy friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing after exposing vulnerability being looked down on or negated, worrying about obtaining negative evaluation
target_behavior.function: Reducing anxiety and shame in the short term, avoiding potential criticism and embarrassment
target_behavior.consequence: Unable to obtain realistic support and corrective information, increasing isolation and maintaining and intensifying self-doubt
